title: Pointwise local-ring criteria for local complete intersections
statement: Let $k$ be a field. For a scheme $X$ locally of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], the following are equivalent: (1) $X$ has an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras that are local complete intersections over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; (2) every point $x\in X$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ such that $R$ is a global complete intersection over $k$; (3) every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $k$, meaning that it is isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to a quotient of a regular local $k$-algebra essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] by an ideal generated by a finite regular sequence [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. For a finitely generated $k$-algebra $S$, $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ if and only if every localization $S_{\mathfrak p}$ at a prime ideal [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a complete-intersection local ring over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Empty schemes and zero rings are allowed.

source.place: Tag 01UG (lemma-local-complete-intersection), equivalence of (1), (2), (3), together with Algebra Tag 00SH (lemma-lci-global), equivalence of (1) and (2). The local-ring definition is Algebra Tag 00SD (definition-lci-local-ring); essentially finite type is Tag 00QM (definition-essentially-finite-p-t).

proof.text: First let $T\ne0$ be a global complete intersection over $k$. Choose its presentation $T\cong Q/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$, $Q=k[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$, with $\dim T=m-c$ from [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. For a prime $\mathfrak a$ of $T$, let $\mathfrak b$ be its inverse image in $Q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], $Q_{\mathfrak b}$ is regular local; it is essentially of finite type by [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. By [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence], the images $f_1/1,\ldots,f_c/1$ form a regular sequence in $Q_{\mathfrak b}$. They lie in its maximal ideal because $f_i\in\mathfrak b$. The map $Q_{\mathfrak b}/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)\to T_{\mathfrak a}$ sends the class of $r/s$ to $\bar r/\bar s$. It is bijective: lift numerator and denominator of a fraction in $T_{\mathfrak a}$ to $Q$, and an element maps to zero exactly when some denominator outside $\mathfrak b$ multiplies its numerator into $(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$. Thus $T_{\mathfrak a}$ is a quotient of a regular local $k$-algebra essentially of finite type by a finite regular sequence in its maximal ideal, and hence a complete-intersection local ring. The zero ring has no primes and contributes no local ring.

source.place: Tags 00S9 (definition-lci-field), 00SB (lemma-lci-CM), 00SC (lemma-lci), last proof paragraph, and 00OQ (proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring); this is the global-to-local direction used by 00SG.

proof.text: Let $S$ be a finitely generated local-complete-intersection $k$-algebra and $\mathfrak q$ a prime. The covering in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] gives $h\notin\mathfrak q$ with $S_h$ global complete intersection. Put $\mathfrak q_h=\{a/h^j:a\in\mathfrak q\}$. The canonical map $S_{\mathfrak q}\to(S_h)_{\mathfrak q_h}$ is an isomorphism: its inverse sends $(a/h^i)/(b/h^j)$ to $ah^j/(h^ib)$, and the forward map sends $a/b$ to $(a/1)/(b/1)$. The fraction relations verify both composites are identities; the maps preserve $k$. Step 1 applied to $S_h$ proves that $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a complete-intersection local ring.

source.place: Tags 00S9 and 00SG (lemma-lci-at-prime): direct use of the defining principal cover and iterated localization.

proof.text: For the reverse direction at a fixed prime, let $S$ be any finitely generated $k$-algebra, $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime, and suppose $A=S_{\mathfrak q}$ is isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to $R/(a_1,\ldots,a_c)$, where $R$ is a regular local $k$-algebra essentially of finite type and $a_1,\ldots,a_c$ is a finite regular sequence in its maximal ideal. Choose algebra generators $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ of $S$. Evaluation gives a surjection $\pi:P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to S$, with kernel $I$, and an isomorphism $P/I\cong S$: evaluation on a polynomial class is well-defined, surjective by the generating property and injective by the definition of $I$. Put $\mathfrak p=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. The map $\alpha:P_{\mathfrak p}\to A$, $r/t\mapsto\pi(r)/\pi(t)$, is surjective, because numerator and denominator in $S_{\mathfrak q}$ lift through $\pi$, and a lifted denominator lies outside $\mathfrak p$. Its kernel is $IP_{\mathfrak p}$: $\pi(r)/\pi(t)=0$ precisely when some $s\notin\mathfrak q$ kills $\pi(r)$; lifting $s$ gives $u\notin\mathfrak p$ with $ur\in I$, hence $r/t=(ur)/(ut)\in IP_{\mathfrak p}$. The converse follows by applying $\alpha$ to a generator of that ideal. The map is local since the inverse image of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ is $\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak p}$. Both $P_{\mathfrak p}$ and $A$ are essentially of finite type directly from the localization definition [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Tag 00SG, condition (4), polynomial presentation and the fraction calculation underlying lemma-lci-local (00SF).

proof.text: Continue with $P,I,S,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q,A$ and $\alpha$ from step 3. The polynomial regular-ring theorem [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring] makes $P_{\mathfrak p}$ regular local. The assumed local complete-intersection presentation of $A$ gives a regular local $k$-algebra $R$, essentially of finite type, and a surjective local $k$-algebra map $R\to A$ whose kernel is generated by a finite regular sequence. Its kernel is proper since $A=S_{\mathfrak q}$ is nonzero, so every element of this generating sequence lies in the maximal ideal of $R$. The two source rings $R$ and $P_{\mathfrak p}$ and the common target $A$ meet every hypothesis of [lem-trf-essentially-finite-type-ci-kernel-invariance]. Applying it to these two surjections shows that $\ker\alpha=IP_{\mathfrak p}$ is generated by a finite regular sequence in $P_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Tag 00SF (lemma-lci-local), (1) implies (2), applied to the chosen polynomial-local presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lci-regular-sequence-global-complete-intersection] to $S=P/I$ using the regular-sequence generation of $IP_{\mathfrak p}$ proved in step 4. Here $P$ is a finite-variable polynomial ring over the same field $k$, and $\mathfrak p$ is exactly the inverse image of the prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$, as required. It gives $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $S_g$ is a global complete intersection over $k$. Thus a complete-intersection local ring at any prime of a finitely generated algebra has a principal global-complete-intersection neighbourhood; this conclusion has been derived from the kernel calculation, rather than assumed as another criterion.

source.place: Tag 00SC (lemma-lci), (5) implies (1), as used in Tag 00SG.

proof.text: If every $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a complete-intersection local ring, steps 3--5 give a $g_{\mathfrak q}\notin\mathfrak q$ for every prime $\mathfrak q$ with $S_{g_{\mathfrak q}}$ global complete intersection. The corresponding $D(g_{\mathfrak q})$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}S$, since $\mathfrak q$ belongs to its own chosen open. This is precisely the definition of local complete intersection in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Together with step 2 it proves the final algebra equivalence in the item. When $S=0$, there are no primes and the empty family covers the empty spectrum; the stipulated zero-ring convention gives the same conclusion.

source.place: Tag 00SH (lemma-lci-global), (1) equivalent to (2), with the principal-cover argument written out; no finite subcover is needed for the recorded definition.

proof.text: For the scheme implication (1) implies (3), fix $x\in X$ and choose a member $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ of the cover in (1) containing $x$. The coordinate algebra $S$ is finitely generated and a local complete intersection by that condition, so step 2 gives the complete-intersection property of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ for the prime corresponding to $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] this localization is $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. The identification preserves $k$: it sends a fraction $r/s$ to $r_xs_x^{-1}$ and thus commutes with the structural map from $k$ to the section ring and then to its germs. Composing the regular-local quotient presentation with this $k$-algebra isomorphism proves (3).

source.place: Tag 01UG (lemma-local-complete-intersection), (1) implies (3), using Algebra 00SH and the affine stalk identification.

proof.text: For (3) implies (2), fix $x\in X$. By the given local finite type hypothesis and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], there is an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ containing $x$ with $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra: use the affine target $\operatorname{Spec}k$ itself in that definition. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], its prime $\mathfrak q$ at $x$ gives $S_{\mathfrak q}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$ as $k$-algebras (the germ formula verifies the scalar compatibility as in step 7). Condition (3) therefore supplies the assumption of step 3. Steps 3--5 produce $g\notin\mathfrak q$ with $S_g$ global complete intersection. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], $D_U(g)$ is an affine open of $X$ containing $x$, and its coordinate ring is $S_g$ through restriction of sections. This is a $k$-algebra identification, since the localization map extends the same structural map $k\to S$. It is the neighbourhood required in (2).

source.place: Tag 01UG (lemma-local-complete-intersection), (3) implies (2), using Algebra 00SG and Schemes Tags 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine) and 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves).

proof.text: Finally (2) implies (1): the neighbourhoods in (2) cover $X$. A global-complete-intersection coordinate algebra $R$ is finitely generated and is also a local complete intersection by [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], taking the single element $1\in R$ so that $D(1)=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $R_1\cong R$. Thus these same neighbourhoods form the cover in (1). The three scheme conditions are equivalent by (1)$\Rightarrow$(3)$\Rightarrow$(2)$\Rightarrow$(1). For $X=\varnothing$, use the empty affine cover and the vacuous pointwise assertions; no zero ring is asserted to be a nonzero local ring.

source.place: Tag 01UG (lemma-local-complete-intersection), (2) implies (1); Algebra Tag 00S9 including the zero-ring convention.
